headline: Writing a URS for a Purified Water system
lead: Your user requirement specification (URS) is your document, answered row by row. Settle what changes design, price and who can bid. First: where our polypropylene package does not fit.

blocks.h: When polypropylene is the wrong choice
blocks.intro: Our package is polypropylene (PP) with polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pretreatment. If your URS needs any row below, our package does not fit as written. We will tell you early.
rows: Water for Injection (WFI), pure steam or a sterile-product loop
Outside this package's scope.
A WFI or stainless steel system supplier
A loop held hot, routine 80 °C sanitization at loop pressure, or steam sterilization
Natural PP is rated 0 to 80 °C, and its pressure rating falls as it heats.
A polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) or stainless loop [whether we quote PVDF]
A chlorine or hypochlorite sanitization you cannot change
Polypropylene is not recommended for chlorinated service.
Another chemical method, if your procedures allow it
A corporate or client standard that names 316L stainless steel
A policy, not a technical question. A deviation needs your quality unit's approval.
A stainless steel system supplier
An extension of a hot-sanitized stainless system
The two parts could not share one sanitization regime.
The existing material
Very small or occasional demand
A generation skid and a loop would be oversized. Our range: [standard platforms and capacity ranges].
Service deionization (exchange tanks) or a laboratory polisher
Equipment outdoors, in an unheated room, or pipe in return-air plenums
Unpigmented PP is sensitive to sunlight, and PP is combustible. Some components need a heated room.
A heated indoor plant room, on a route your code accepts

blocks.h: What a Purified Water URS should settle
blocks.intro: Number each requirement, one sentence each. Suppliers answer in your numbering; evaluators score the same rows.

items.d: Feed water, grade, demand and site limits first. Then the loop: scheme, components, check against URS and budget, change or freeze.
items.label: Start

items.d: Purified Water to USP, Ph. Eur. or both, by edition. Say where the system starts and ends, and what is by others.
items.label: Grade

items.d: List every point of use, washers and humidifiers too. Give peak draw in L/h, daily volume, temperature and planned growth.
items.label: Demand

items.d: Attach feed water analyses from every season, and the coldest feed temperature. Cold feed cuts membrane output.
items.label: Feed

items.t: Quality limits and where you prove them
items.d: Name each limit and its pharmacopoeia. Say where it is measured, online or in the lab, and who sets alert and action levels.
items.label: Limits

items.d: Settle the sanitization method first: it decides the materials. Then write materials as performance, unless a standard names one.
items.label: Sanitize

items.d: Where failed water goes, restart after a power cut, user access, audit trail, data retention and backup, and screen language.
items.label: Controls

items.d: Room size and access, power, air, drains and room temperature. Name who obtains each Canadian approval, such as pressure registration.
items.label: Site

items.d: Who writes and approves each protocol, and whether factory test results count toward qualification. Define acceptance: tests, run length, signatures.
items.label: Tests

items.d: A dated document schedule, the handover set, response hours, spares on site, training hours and the warranty start event.
items.label: Handover

blocks.h: Must-haves, preferences and how bids answer
cols: What it does to the bids
rows: Must-have
One shortfall ends a bid, whatever its price.
What your product, your inspector or a written standard requires
Preference
Scored against the other bids.
Features you would trade for price, time or service
Too many must-haves
Fewer suppliers can bid; sometimes only one is left.
Ask of each one: is this the outcome, or one way to reach it?
One answer format
Every row answered: meets, meets with a note, or differs, with the proving document.
Every row of the URS
One deviation list
Silence is often read as full compliance, and enforced later.
Every difference, keyed to your row numbers, with its reason
Separate price lines
Shows what each bid includes, and lets you trim options to your budget.
Factory and site tests, documents, start-up, training, spares and options

blocks.h: Clauses that keep the design open
blocks.intro: A clause that names hardware decides the design before anyone has seen your plant. If you truly need one material or method, say so plainly.
cols: Outcome clause any supplier can answer
rows: An analyser of one named make and model
Monitoring
Online conductivity at the loop return within the pharmacopoeia limit, with calibration records
316L stainless steel for all product-contact parts
Product contact
Compatible with Purified Water and your sanitizing agent, certified by lot, fully drainable, with minimal dead legs
Hot-water sanitization at 80 °C, weekly
Sanitization
Method and frequency to suit the materials, proven effective in every part; any chemical sanitant proven absent before use
Orbital welds with weld logs and borescope records
Joints
A record traceable to each joint, with its examination and acceptance

blocks.h: Rows to write if you allow polypropylene
blocks.intro: Written this way, a polypropylene bid can be scored, not excluded. Each row can be checked at installation.
rows: Product-contact material
Virgin, unpigmented polypropylene, with a material certificate per lot
Purified Water quality and your sanitizing agent
Pressure rating and wall
Pressure class and wall ratio for each line, stated at your highest operating and sanitizing temperature
Polypropylene's pressure rating falls as it heats
Joints and records
A record per joint, with a joint map and examination, replacing stainless weld logs and passivation records
A stainless document list copied into a plastic URS leaves rows nobody can answer
Sanitization
A method within the material's temperature and chemical ratings; any sanitant proven absent at every outlet before use
Your sanitization procedure and the material maker's chemical resistance data
Installation
Tank and pipe kept from sunlight, in a heated room, on supports that let the pipe expand
Unpigmented polypropylene is sensitive to sunlight; plastic pipe moves more with temperature than steel

blocks.h: Writing a specification section instead of a URS
blocks.intro: Consultants often issue a three-part specification section with the drawings. The same rules apply: outcomes, must-haves marked, and who does what.
rows: What you receive from us
A compliance matrix against your client's URS, within [compliance matrix response time, working days]
Basis of design at the concept hold. Diagrams and a draft functional specification at basic design; approved issues at detailed design.

rows.intent: I have a URS or a draft|Compliance matrix

rows: Part 1 General
Scope, references, submittals, quality, warranty and its start event
Cite GUI-0001 first, then the pharmacopoeia and edition you release to
Part 2 Products
Performance rows, with a basis of design "or approved equal"
Write outcomes; name a material only when a standard requires one
Part 3 Execution
Installation, field joints, flushing, testing, start-up and training
Say who does each: package supplier, contractor or owner
Building commissioning
Utilities, building automation points and the plant room
A separate layer from the water system's own qualification

items.q: Who writes the URS, and who answers it?
items.a: You write it, and your quality unit approves it. A consultant may draft it for you; the approval stays yours. Suppliers answer it row by row, and the answers often become part of the contract.

items.q: Can we send our URS before we issue it?
items.a: Yes. A draft is the best time: a sentence costs less to change than a design. We mark each gap and propose wording. Your URS stays yours to write and approve.
items.intent: I have a URS or a draft|URS gap review

items.q: Will a review from you tie our URS to Aquemi?
items.a: No. We propose outcome wording that any capable supplier can answer. Where a row fits only one design, we mark it. Where polypropylene is the wrong choice, we say so.

items.q: Our corporate standard names stainless steel. Can polypropylene still bid?
items.a: Only with a deviation your quality unit approves. If the standard stands, write it as a must-have and ask stainless suppliers. That saves everyone a bid.

items.q: Which standards should our URS cite?
items.a: In Canada, Health Canada's GUI-0001 first. Then the pharmacopoeia you release to, USP or Ph. Eur., with its edition. USP <1231> is guidance, not a requirement. For design, WHO TRS 1033 Annex 3 is a common reference. Name the text, never "pharma grade".

items.q: We are a small firm. How long should our URS be?
items.a: As long as its rows need. A short URS that settles grade, demand, feed water, sanitization and acceptance beats a long copied one. Buying your first system? Start with the plain guide.
